title: Sound the Alarm
subtitle: Ultimately, there is always more than one weather forecaster.

trails.title: IDM Maintenance Records
trails.description: A page torn from a machine maintenance log, creased from having been repeatedly unfolded and folded.

content.text:
November 8 Replaced punched paper cards. No equipment abnormalities.

November 9 Shutdown for 30 minutes to check the connector board. Inspection results: some wires slightly aged; no leakage or poor contact was detected. Reported and added wires to the monthly off-island purchase list.

November 10 Shutdown for 30 minutes to check the motor drive. Inspection results: performance good.

November 11 Shutdown for 30 minutes to check the indicator device. Inspection results: the needle of meter a1G4 was stuck; upon troubleshooting, the internal gears of meter a1G4 were corroded. Reported and added the indicator meter to the monthly off-island purchase list.

November 12 Replaced punched paper cards. No equipment abnormalities.

November 13 No equipment abnormalities.

November 14 No equipment abnormalities.

November 15 Shutdown for 1 hour 15 minutes to replace the meter. Also obtained a new type of connector board from off the island, scheduled to be replaced the next day.

November 16 Replaced punched paper cards. No equipment abnormalities.

November 17 Replaced the new connector board. Shutdown for 3 hours, replacement completed.

November 18 No equipment abnormalities. Disposal of the original connector board: I gave it to my daughter, Sophia, who is quite fond of studying these. The disposal has been approved.

November 19 No equipment abnormalities.

November 20 Replaced the punched paper cards. No equipment abnormalities.

items.text: Sound the Alarm
Laboratory, Island

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What, what am I looking at?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: So your so-called sacred project is this gigantic IDM computer?
Regulus inspects the computer like an expert.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I was curious about them during my stay in Laplace. Those later versions of the model are so much better than the 66 ones!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But this one doesn't seem that far advanced to those. This is not a junk piece the Manus sold you, is it?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Items of the phenomenal world are all a waste.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This one is long broken. After the Emanation, we couldn't find anyone to repair it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why do you keep referring to the "Storm" as the Emanation?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What does the Emanation mean?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It is the waves of pneuma.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: We are the expellees of the world of Forms. We were banished to this damp and dark cave.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Everyone here is obsessed with the fake light on the wall but forgets to look for the truth.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Pneuma, however, will lead us to escape the cave and return to a more supreme realm.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ehh! You make it sound like we are living in piles of rubbish!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Aren't we?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Of course not!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: If you ask me, I'd say you have absolutely no idea how wonderful the outside world is, because you have never left here to try it yourself!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Dr. Papper, the music festivals, Rory Storm, The Hollies, and the Rolling Stones ... There are too many to count!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: If it weren't for this sick "Storm," I would still be riding a motorcycle in one of those races in London!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm, your soul must be pretty contaminated.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: And the computer! They can calculate extremely large numbers within seconds, better than hundreds of thousands of you combined together!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: In the case of numbers, it's not "the bigger, the better."

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Also, this computer has never played a useful part in our study.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Come on, mate! You people just leave it in a cave! It's like sending an infant to the kitchen and waiting for it to bring you dinner!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Never mind. You'll see what I mean after I fix it.
Regulus mutters as she gets down on the ground and crawls closer to the computer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Can you fix an IDM, Regulus?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: No. But I've seen the Laplace people do it. Shouldn't be too difficult, I assume.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Urgh, the dust! When was the last time you sent people down here to clean?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Aw, some critters are nesting here! Oh, did I break into your party?!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin, come give me a hand! They won't let me touch 'em!
Green numbers appear on the screen.
After getting rid of the parasitic pests, the dusty behemoth begins to miraculously return to life.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You fixed it!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: It's great to have you clean the laboratory, Regulus! Your floating point immediately reduced!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah, is that a compliment? Sounds like one to me. Thank you!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It's a wordplay, Captain. Infinity minus any numbers still equals to infinity.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh! Fine, fine! I should have given up the idea of changing your eccentric sorting system a long time ago.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What's the meaning of humans inventing computers, if these machines were only left here for some critters to nest in?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Thanks to you, now we can have a look at the previous models, Regulus.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: But it's a pity since it only has the data before 2003. Everything in the past four years has gone missing.
37's fingers are dancing over the keyboard; she seems surprisingly familiar with operating this computer.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: This is our chronology, Vertin.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: From 1999 to 2007, the Emanation has taken place seven times.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: In the initial four years, the Emanation has a pattern. First, it brought us back to the 90s, then the 80s, and then the 70s.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: After that, it suddenly leaped to the 30s. In the subsequent three years, it took place twice.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Every record here can perfectly match what is in the Foundation's files.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait. These are the records before 2003, you say?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But this one refers to the "Storm" in 1966, which happened recently!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: These are indeed the records before 2003.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: What's following the records is our forecast.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huuhh! That's to say, you prophesied the 1966 "Storm" four years prior to its occurrence?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: How is this possible ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: … that you are clever enough to develop such a precise mathematical model, while at the same time you just let the IDM become the home of these critters?!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: We just worked out the patterns in the number sequences.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You made such a precise prediction even without leaving the island! Huh, that's incredible!
37's lips curl unhappily.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: You don't need to go into a river to find out the pattern of its flow.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Moreover, we would send people to observe in the phenomenal world. My mother was one of them.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: She is the co-author of this model. Nobody knows this computer better than her.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: So, you have a mother, too?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Too?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: 37, where is your mother now?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Like many people, she was restored to her true Form. Since then, I took over this laboratory.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The "Form" you said ... 37, what is it?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: What kind of question is this?
She tilts her head, looking genuinely confused.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The Form, or the essence, is what's left of you after all the fakeness has been peeled off.
TO BE CONTINUED…
